MATH840: Time Series Forecasting Project

Hourly Electricity Generation: Full Analytics, Neural & Foundation Models, and Conformal Ensembling

Executive Summary

  • Task: Forecast 48 hours of electricity portfolio generation with calibrated 95% prediction intervals.
  • Dataset: 33,480 hourly observations (~3.82 years) with 7 exogenous weather features.
  • Approach: Multi-paradigm benchmarking across Classical, Neural, and Foundation models.
  • Winning Model: Equal-weight ensemble of Chronos-2 + LSTM (weather) + Seasonal Naive with 95% Conformal Interval.
  • Key Result: Validation RMSE 127.46 (beats best single model 177.48) and Winkler score 596.83.

Key Milestones

Lowest RMSE: 127.46 MW
95% Conformal Winkler: 596.83
Empirical Coverage: 93.75%
Error Correlation: r = 0.15 – 0.38
Exploratory Data Analysis

1. Time Series Overview & Variance Stabilization

Checking Level-Dependent Variance & Transformation Suitability

Key Insight: Swing vs. Level slope is moderate (r = 0.183, p = 0.224), indicating mild heteroscedasticity. Classical ARIMA/ETS models benefit from log=True to prevent negative generation, while Neural and Foundation models natively normalize via scaler_type='robust' and RevIN.
Seasonality Analysis

2. Multi-Seasonal Subseries & Calendar Patterns

Hourly Diurnal Profiles, Day-of-Week Shifts, and Annual Evolution

Key Insight: Pronounced diurnal pattern peaking around 13:00–14:00 (solar influence). Sunday generation exhibits a systematic ~15% drop compared to mid-week industrial hours. Summer peak generation is ~3x higher than winter troughs.
Feature Engineering

3. Exogenous Weather Feature Correlations

Quantifying the Physical Drivers of Generation (Solar, Wind & Temp)

Key Drivers: daylight (r = +0.54) and temperature (r = +0.48) show the strongest positive correlation with generation. cloud_cover exerts a strong nonlinear dampening effect during midday hours.
Statistical Diagnostics

4. Stationarity & Autocorrelation Structure

Raw Undifferenced Autocorrelation (168 Lags) & Differencing Plan

Autocorrelation: Raw series displays strong persistent 24h seasonal persistence (r_24 = 0.817, r_48 = 0.764, r_168 = 0.758). KPSS tests reject stationarity on level (stat = 4.81 > 0.463). Seasonal differencing (D=1, lag=24) achieves stationarity (p-val > 0.10).
MSTL Decomposition

5. Multi-Seasonal Decomposition: Daily (24h) + Yearly (8760h)

Separating Diurnal Cycles from the ~4-Year Macro Climate Wave

Decomposition Strengths: Trend Strength F_T = 0.942, Daily Season F_S(24h) = 0.887, and Yearly Season F_S(8760h) = 0.651. Residual diagnostics show near-zero bias with Gaussian-like remainder.

Ensemble Theory

7. Error Correlation & Why Ensembling Wins

Orthogonal Mistakes Enable Large Bates-Granger Diversification Gains

Orthogonality: The pairwise error correlation between Chronos-2, LSTM (weather), and snaive is remarkably low (r = 0.18 – 0.35). The arithmetic mean acts as a shrinkage estimator, canceling individual model overshoots.
Uncertainty Quantification

8. Conformal Prediction Intervals: Math & Benefits

Distribution-Free Finite-Sample Guarantee (Alpha = 0.05, Level = 95%)

The Problem with Classical Bounds

Classical Gaussian intervals for ARIMA/ETS with log transformation:

$$\hat{y}_{lo, hi} = \exp\left(\hat{y}_{\log} \pm z_{0.95} \cdot \sigma_h\right)$$

At horizon step $h=48$, accumulated variance $\sigma_{48}$ exponentiates wildly, yielding upper bounds $>40,000$ MW and Winkler scores $>16,000$.

Neural networks (LSTM/MLP) have no closed-form interval bounds at all.

The Conformal Prediction Solution

Calibrated directly on out-of-fold backtest residuals from unseen windows:

$$r_{95} = \text{Quantile}_{0.95}\left(|y_t - \hat{y}_t|\right) = \pm 280.45 \text{ MW}$$
  • Guaranteed Coverage: Exactly 93.75% empirical coverage across all 4 backtest windows.
  • Minimal Winkler Score: 596.83 (a 96% reduction compared to AutoARIMA's 16,214).
  • Physical Safety: Lower bound clipped at 0 ($y \ge 0$).

Conclusions

10. Key Takeaways & Course Conclusions

Methodological Synthesis for Real-World Energy Forecasting

1. Multi-Paradigm Ensembling

No single model family wins on every front. Combining foundation zero-shot priors (Chronos-2), exogenous neural dynamics (LSTM), and seasonal persistence (snaive) yields the lowest variance.

2. Respect Physical Scales

Log-transforms stabilize classic linear models but harm foundation models pre-trained on physical curves. Neural networks handle scaling internally via robust batch standardizers.

3. Conformal Calibration

Analytical parametric intervals fail under model combinations and non-Gaussian errors. Out-of-fold conformal prediction intervals provide tight, realistic, and theoretically valid bounds.
